messages:
ben-cust: Hey @support, since we flipped the corp inspection proxy chain our Private deployment can't reach the control plane. API calls timeout or show TLS errors. Seeing spike in 502s and 524s from our side.

alice-support: Hi Ben — sorry you're hitting this. Quick Qs: is this the on-prem env behind the dual proxy (edge NTLM -> TLS inspection)? Any curl -v or openssl output you can paste?

ben-cust: Yes exactly: edge proxy does NTLM auth, then inspection appliance does TLS MITM. Here's the minimal curl we tried:

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
*   Trying 10.20.30.40:443...
* Connected to api.redwood.example (10.20.30.40) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: SSL: certificate subject name 'inspector.local' does not match 'api.redwood.example'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name 'inspector.local' does not match 'api.redwood.example'
```

ben-cust: We also see intermittent ECONNRESET from our side.

carla-sre: That output suggests your inspection device is doing TLS termination and presenting its own cert (inspector.local). Two likely issues: 1) split-horizon DNS pointing api.redwood.example at an internal IP (10.20.30.40), or 2) proxy rewrites SNI/Host or terminates TLS. Can you run: `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -servername api.redwood.example -showcerts` and paste result? Also paste `nslookup api.redwood.example` on one of your app hosts.

ben-cust: nslookup output below:

```
Server: 10.10.0.2
Address: 10.10.0.2#53

Name: api.redwood.example
Address: 10.20.30.40
```

ben-cust: openssl s_client shows the inspector cert CN=inspector.local, issuer our corp CA. So DNS resolves to internal egress gateway that terminates TLS.

diane-platform: Thanks — that confirms split-horizon DNS + TLS inspect. Two important callouts: 1) Our control plane expects TLS passthrough to present Redwood certs; MITM with a corp CA will break cert validation for clients that verify server certs. 2) Even if you accept the MITM cert, some TLS features (ALPN, SNI) may be altered and break HTTP/2 streaming or token-based connection upgrades.

alice-support: Can you try a quick repro to confirm DNS is the root cause? Run this from an app host: `curl --resolve api.redwood.example:443:198.51.100.23 https://api.redwood.example/v1/health -I` (replace 198.51.100.23 with our public egress IP we provided earlier). If that succeeds, it's DNS/proxy related.

ben-cust: Ran that — returns HTTP/1.1 200 OK when using --resolve. So direct to public works. Normal path fails.

carla-sre: Good repro. That means your inspection/proxy chain is intercepting TLS. Two remediation paths:
- Preferred: configure your edge/inspection policy to use CONNECT tunneling / SSL passthrough for our service hostnames or IP ranges (198.51.100.0/24). This preserves SNI and cert.
- If passthrough is impossible: you must ensure the inspection device forwards original SNI and ALPN, and allow outbound OCSP/CRL to our cert issuing CA. Alternatively, issue a cookie to your clients to bypass inspect for API calls.

alice-support: I'll add a docs pointer for our recommended squid/proxy settings and for the required egress IP ranges. Also: ensure your firewall/egress allowlist permits outbound to port 443 for our control-plane IPs and to ocsp.redwood.com:80 for cert checks.

ben-cust: Any quick config snippets? Our team uses Squid + NTLM.

diane-platform: Example (squid) to force CONNECT for our hostnames:

```
acl redwood_hosts dstdomain .api.redwood.example .api.redwood-public.com
http_access deny !Safe_ports
http_access deny CONNECT !SSL_ports
acl CONNECT_SSL port 443
http_access allow redwood_hosts CONNECT_SSL
cache_peer 0.0.0.0 parent 3128 0 no-query no-digest no-netdb-exchange no-cache
# ensure SSL bump is disabled for redwood hosts
ssl_bump splice redwood_hosts
```

carla-sre: And if you run a transparent TLS-inspect appliance, add an exception to not rewrite SNI/Host for our domains. Otherwise the proxy will present corp certs and any client doing strict validation will fail.

ben-cust: We also noticed some token auth failures and billing spikes after the change. Could the MITM cause auth breaks?

alice-support: Token auth is independent of TLS, but if your clients are failing TLS and retrying across many endpoints, you could see duplicate requests that look like increased usage. Also if our control plane sees a bunch of requests from the same NAT'd egress IP it can trigger rate limiting which shows as 429/5xx on the client and can look like auth issues.

ben-cust: We captured a tcpdump showing RSTs inserted by the inspector after ClientHello in ~40ms. Should we escalate to network infra?

carla-sre: Yes please open a ticket with your network team and request they: 1) verify that SNI is not rewritten for redwood hosts, 2) enable CONNECT/SSL passthrough for our IP ranges, 3) allow outbound ocsp/ca CRL queries. We can provide the IP ranges and an ephemeral test cert if they want to validate passthrough behavior.

alice-support: I'll attach a short checklist and the IP ranges: `198.51.100.0/24`, `203.0.113.0/24` (example ranges). Also we recommend a short maintenance window to remove the exception after testing.

ben-cust: Thanks — we'll try the CONNECT rule and test. One more: our egress uses an auth refresh proxy that inserts Proxy-Authorization header. Could that break things?

diane-platform: Proxy auth headers are fine for HTTP proxying, but for HTTPS you should not perform header injection on the CONNECT tunnel. If the proxy rewrites Host or inserts headers before establishing TLS, it can break our mutual expectations.

support-bot: ACTIONS: (1) ben-cust to request passthrough/CONNECT exception with infra and share screenshots of failing curl. (2) alice-support to provide IP ranges + docs link and follow up in 24h. (3) carla-sre to standby for packet capture review if infra applies changes.

ben-cust: Opening infra ticket now, will paste updates. Thanks all :thumbsup:

alice-support: Great — ping here when infra confirms config and we'll re-run tests. If they need a temporary bypass, we can open a support case to whitelist a specific egress IP for a short window.

carla-sre: FYI — if your org cannot disable TLS inspect for compliance reasons, you can run our Private control plane over an IPsec/VPN tunnel or use our Dedicated mode with a static private peering IP. DM me and I can loop in solutions engineering.

ben-cust: Noted. I'll update after infra ticket. Appreciate the quick help.

support-bot: thread archived (will reopen on update)
